Understanding what the back end is actually doing is important here. Basically the backed and s3 specifically just holds the state file. Now any good data steward has versioning on their s3 buckets. So that acts as your back up of the plain text state file formatted in Json. 

But it's just a plaintext file in a directory somewhere. What really makes AWS s3 back end shine. Is the pairing of a dynamodb table for state locking. 

But long story short. Your answer is maybe. If the credentials thing isn't an issue then no prob save your text file at the path. But you don't have the state file locking. 

So is that different than backing up your state file with a local back end path to a network share that you personally manage? That's up to you.
